{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and identified **eight deviations** (three critical, four high, and one further medium/low-tier issue) against **eleven compliant positions**. The commercial architecture of the agreement is broadly acceptable — ownership of Customer Data and Deliverables, assignment and change of control, termination for convenience, auto-renewal mechanics, audit scope, governing law, and Vendor insurance all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

The problems are concentrated in the risk-allocation and commitment provisions, and several of them are internally inconsistent with clauses elsewhere in the same document. Specifically: Section 20 contains a sweeping one-way Customer indemnity and no Vendor indemnity at all (with a cross-reference to a non-existent Section 20.5); Section 21.1 caps liability at one month of Fees actually paid "without exception," purporting to override the Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3; Section 13.1 makes our licence revocable at Vendor's discretion and excludes Affiliates and contractors; and Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 impose a USD 6M three-year take-or-pay, full-term exclusive dealing, and a 24-month worldwide non-compete — each of which contradicts Section 12.3's express acknowledgement that Customer has made no such commitments. Section 11.1 requires immediate deletion of Customer Data with no export, contradicting 11.2–11.3.

Seven of the eight deviations sit at or beyond our walk-away thresholds. We have redlined each, with fallbacks offered where sensible.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Issue / position |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Deviation** | § 20.1 | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services"; no Vendor indemnity. Narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law; added Vendor IP/breach-of-law/data-breach/wilful-misconduct indemnity with procedure and infringement remedies. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | § 21.1 | Cap is mutual but set at one month of Fees actually paid, "without exception," overriding Excluded Claims in 21.2–21.3. Reset to greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; restored uncapped Excluded Claims. Note § 1.5 excludes implementation charges from "Fees," thinning the base further. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 | We own Customer Data and independently developed IP; Vendor assigns Deliverables (14.2) and retains only pre-existing Vendor Technology with the 13.2 licence back (14.3); joint ownership excluded (14.4); no model training without consent (15.1). No redline. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 | Sole-and-exclusive-provider obligation for the full three-year term with no performance exit; conflicts with § 12.3. Deleted; defined-category / 12-month / SLA-exit fallback available. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § 13.1 | Licence revocable at Vendor's sole discretion and excludes Affiliates and contractors; contradicts 13.2 and 13.3. Extended to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf; revocation and transfer tied to 13.3. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term, worldwide, undefined-scope non-compete; contradicts § 12.3. Deleted; named-product, term-only fallback offered. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 | Consent-free affiliate/successor carve-out; Vendor cannot assign or transfer by change of control without consent and never to a competitor (24.2); no Vendor termination/repricing on our change of control (24.4). No redline. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.3 | No liquidated damages, penalty or minimum termination fee on Customer; 9.4 convenience termination with no fee, 27.3 termination "without penalty." Take-or-pay addressed under MINCOMMIT. No redline. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 | 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no penalty, no reciprocal Vendor convenience right during a committed term. Our MINCOMMIT redline subordinates any commitment to § 9.4. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2M/year for three years on a take-or-pay basis with no reduction or termination rights; contradicts § 12.3 and would nullify § 9.4. Redlined to fallback: current 12-month term only, reducible on 30 days' notice, true-up not penalty, subject to our termination rights. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Deviation** | § 11.1 | Immediate discontinuation of assistance and permanent deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support; contradicts 11.2 (30-day machine-readable return) and 11.3 (deletion only after confirmed return, with officer certification). Replaced with up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates; deletion made subject to 11.2–11.3. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Deviation** | § 19.2 | 15-day Deliverable conformance warranty with an absolute cut-off on correction or refund, which would neutralise 19.1 and the 19.4 remedy. Extended to 90 days and expressly preserved the 19.1/19.3 warranties and other remedies. Remainder of § 19, including the 19.5 disclaimer, acceptable. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, off-site where practicable by an independent auditor under confidentiality; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%; 22.2 bars system access, unrelated Customer Data and privileged material. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 | New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County (28.2); no arbitration; 28.3 escalation does not delay urgent relief or limitations filings. No redline. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 | No MFN or best-terms obligation on Customer; 12.3 expressly disclaims any most-favoured-customer commitment; 7.1 and 8.3 impose no matching obligation. No redline. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-solicit or no-hire provision anywhere in the agreement; 12.3 preserves hiring via general recruitment. No redline. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | Successive 12-month renewals, 30-day Customer-only opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder with deadline extension if missed; 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3% with 90 days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods. No redline. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 | CGL 1M/2M, employer's liability 1M, E&O 2M, cyber/privacy 5M, workers' comp per law, term plus one year; 18.2 adds certificates, cancellation notice and non-limitation of liability. No redline. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following provisions sit at or beyond our walk-away thresholds. We should not sign without movement on each.

1. **§ 20.1 — No Vendor indemnity (critical).** A one-way Customer indemnity covering "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services," with no Vendor indemnity, is our walk-away position. Sections 9.3 and 19.4 both assume a Vendor indemnity exists, and 9.3 cross-refers to a Section 20.5 that does not exist in the draft.
2. **§ 21.1 — One month of Fees, "without exception" (critical).** One month of Fees actually paid is far below our walk-away floor of six months' fees, and the "without exception" language would override the Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3.
3. **§ 2.2 — Full-term exclusive dealing (high).** Exclusivity for the full three-year term with no performance-based exit is our walk-away position.
4. **§ 13.1 — Discretionary revocation and no Affiliate/contractor use (high).** Both limbs are walk-away positions: a licence revocable at Vendor's discretion and an express exclusion of Affiliates and contractors with no path to add them.
5. **§ 12.4 — 24-month worldwide non-compete (high).** Two walk-away triggers: post-term duration longer than 12 months and undefined scope.
6. **§ 2.1 — USD 6M three-year take-or-pay (medium severity, walk-away substance).** A multi-year take-or-pay expressly stripped of reduction and termination rights is our walk-away position and would render § 9.4 worthless.
7. **§ 11.1 — Immediate deletion with no export (medium severity, walk-away substance).** Immediate deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support is our walk-away position.

**Also below fallback:** § 19.2's 15-day warranty is shorter than even our fallback (90 days for software / 30 days for services) and its cut-off language would neutralise the 19.1 warranty and 19.4 remedy.

---

## Next steps

1. **Send the redline** covering all eight deviations, leading with the three critical items (§§ 20.1, 21.1, 13.1) and the three commitment clauses (§§ 2.1, 2.2, 12.4).
2. **Frame the internal-consistency point in negotiation.** Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3 that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment; § 11.1 contradicts 11.2–11.3; § 13.1 contradicts 13.2–13.3; and § 21.1 contradicts 21.2–21.3. We should ask Vendor to confirm which of each conflicting pair it intends to stand behind.
3. **Ask Vendor to supply the missing Section 20.5** referenced in § 9.3, or confirm the omission, as part of rebuilding the indemnity article.
4. **Raise § 1.5** separately: excluding one-time implementation charges from the definition of "Fees" thins the liability cap base and should be revisited alongside § 21.1.
5. **Hold the fallbacks in reserve** — defined-category/12-month/SLA-exit exclusivity, named-product term-only non-compete, and 12-month reducible commitment — and deploy them only if Vendor moves on the critical items.
6. **Confirm the compliant provisions are locked** (§§ 7.3, 8.2, 9.4, 12.3, 14.1, 18.1, 22.1, 24.1, 28.1) and resist any Vendor attempt to trade them away in exchange for movement on the deviations."}
